title: Tiny Robots That Help Melt Blood Clots
summary: Scientists have made tiny robots that can tumble through your blood. They may help doctors melt blood clots much faster. A blood clot is a lump of blood that blocks a blood vessel. If it is not treated, it can cause a heart attack or a stroke. Doctors use drugs to melt clots. But it is hard to get the drug to the clot. The tiny robots can help. Each robot is shaped like a bullet. It has a magnetic backbone made of iron. A magnet outside the body makes the robots spin and tumble. As they tumble, they push the drug right to the clot. The idea came from tiny bacteria that use magnets in their bodies to find their way. In tests, the robots helped melt clots about 10 times faster than the drug alone. The tests were done first in a model blood vessel, then in live pigs. The scientists still need to test the robots more before they can be used in people.
why_it_matters: Blood clots can hurt people badly, so faster treatment could save lives.
